key: Think of a family WhatsApp group planning a wedding
name: ch09_family_chat_hall_consensus
alt: Family members in different homes all agree on one wedding hall, pinned and padlocked on a shared notice board, while an uncle's phone lies switched off.
scene: A wide illustration of one big family planning a wedding from four different places, arranged around a central wall. In the centre stands a large cork notice board on a cream wall, with one photo card of a wedding hall with a domed roof and marigold garlands pinned at its middle, a big green tick beside it and a brass padlock hanging from the card's corner to show the choice can no longer be changed; two other hall cards lie crossed out at the board's lower edge. Around the board, four family members each hold a phone: on the left a mother in a yellow cotton sari in her kitchen, smiling and pointing at the board; beside her a young cousin in a hoodie on a college bench giving a thumbs-up; on the right a grandfather in a white kurta and spectacles on a cane chair nodding; and in the lower right corner an uncle in a striped shirt snoring on a sofa, his phone lying dark on the cushion with a small zzz cloud and a battery-empty icon, yet the board still shows the same hall. Thin dotted lines run from each awake phone to the single board, so everyone is clearly looking at one place. Warm evening light, cheerful mood. Labels: "CONSENSUS" across the top centre, and "ONE HALL" on a small ribbon under the pinned hall card.

key: Serializability is like an exam hall where answer sheets
name: ch09_exam_hall_clock
alt: Left, an examiner grades a shuffled stack of answer sheets in any order; right, students read the big hall clock and a later reader can never see an earlier time.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same school exam hall, divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: at a wooden desk at the front of the hall, a middle-aged examiner in a grey sweater and spectacles grades a stack of answer sheets; three sheets float above the desk with big numbers 3, 1 and 2 on their corners, and curved arrows show him dealing them into a neat pile in that shuffled order, a red pen in his hand, calm and unbothered, because any single order is fine as long as the sheets are graded one after another. Behind him, rows of empty benches. RIGHT panel: a big round wall clock high on the hall wall, hands at five past ten, with "10:05" written in a small bubble under it. Below, two students at their benches look up at it one after the other: a girl in a school uniform with plaits has just read it and has a green tick beside her; a boy in a white shirt looks up a moment later, and a thought bubble above him showing "10:04" is crossed out with a red X, because once someone has read 10:05, nobody reading afterwards may see an earlier time. A dotted arrow runs from the girl to the boy to show who looked first. Morning light through tall windows, quiet exam mood. Labels: "SERIALIZABLE" at the top of the left panel, and "LINEARIZABLE" at the top of the right panel.
